steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every concern they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Have you been getting headaches?

Have you noticed fatigue or low energy?

How's your sleep been?

Any allergies or sinus stuff?

Have you noticed more stress or irritability?

Are you having any tension, pain, or soreness?

Are you taking any medications for these concerns?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}. This helps us get ready for your visit.

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's exactly what the {{offer_name}} is for. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If chiropractic care can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Objection: Injections or Surgery
steps.content:
Okay. That tells me it's gotten bad enough that you want it handled.

Has a doctor recommended that, or is it something you're looking into yourself?

(Let them answer. Do not talk down injections or surgery.)

Both of those are real options, and sometimes they're the right call. They're also hard to undo once you've done them. A visit with {{provider_name}} doesn't rule anything out. It gives you a second look at {{main_concern}} before you commit to something permanent.

If chiropractic care isn't the answer here, we'll say so. Either way you'll walk into that decision knowing more than you do today.

Does it make sense to get that second look first?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m managing on my own”
steps.content:
Good for you, {{contact_first_name}}. That takes some discipline.

What have you been doing for it?

(Let them answer. Give them credit for it.)

That's getting you through the day, and that matters. What it can't do is tell you why {{main_concern}} keeps coming back. Managing something and fixing it are two different things.

A check with {{provider_name}} tells you which one you're dealing with. If what you're doing is enough, we'll tell you to keep going. If it isn't, you'll find out now instead of a year from now.

Would it help to know for sure?
